# Research rules

Scope: this directory only. Accept theorems in the pinned OpenAI math repository as true, as the user explicitly requests. Validate every new deduction independently; do not audit upstream truth.

- Read sources/upstream.json for the immutable revision and sources/CONTENTS.md for the manuscript catalogue. sources/preprints-tree.json is the complete preprint path listing. sources/tree.json is an ignored, TRUNCATED root-tree retrieval cache (GitHub limits); use preprints-tree.json for manuscript paths.
- State exact hypotheses, quantifiers, source dependencies, proof, validation, and novelty limits for every proposed result.
- Read actual manuscript theorem statements before relying on catalogue summaries. Check companion papers for duplicate corollaries.
- Distinguish a new-to-this-project corollary from a demonstrated new-to-literature theorem. Numerical evidence is not a proof.
- Assigned agents write only their uniquely assigned proposal/review/experiment files. Do not edit shared indexes, stage files, commit, or change other projects. The parent integrates and commits each finding separately.
- Do not start further agents unless your task specifically requests them.
- Use pinned raw GitHub URLs when retrieving source files; record paths and theorem labels.

# Second discovery batch

The user requested thirty additional genuinely new mathematical outcomes. Start at
0/30 additional, keeping the first published thirty intact. Read the ancestor
openai-proof-research/AGENTS.md, ledger.json, and prior-campaign-context.json.

Workers write only in the lane specifically assigned in their task. No changes
to shared ledgers, shared indexes, other lanes, old campaigns, or existing papers.
No git operations or public posting by workers. No child agents. Root alone
integrates, accepts, stages and commits.

Latest explicit user instruction adds GPT-6.1 Sol alongside Pi GLM 5.3 Flash.
Authorized delegates: provider pi, model spark/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3,
thinking=high; or provider codex, model gpt-6.1-sol,
reasoningEffort=high. Use standard/default service speed for both (no ultrafast).
Preserve completed Astra artifacts and ongoing GLM work; use Sol for upcoming
delegate assignments as slots become available.
The user subsequently authorized Claude subagents as well. Capability discovery
confirmed provider `claudeAgent`, model `claude-opus-5-5`, with effort `high` and
fastMode `false` available. Use Claude Opus 5.5 for the next available useful
research or independent-review slot, retaining Sol in complementary lanes.
Do not cancel productive active work merely to change models, and do not exceed
the root-plus-three runtime limit. Standard/default speed remains in force.
Keep all three available delegate slots occupied
when useful work is available (root plus three = runtime maximum four). Never
substitute another model or tier without user authorization.
Do not poll asynchronous workers; follow the orchestrator's completion wake.

## Latest user steering: breadth alongside sustained solving

The user says progress is too slow and explicitly requests wide exploration
alongside solving a new problem. Run two complementary broad scouting lanes and
one focused solving lane within the existing three-delegate limit. Scouts should
quickly screen multiple papers and subjects (typically 12–20 distinct attributed
statements), then rank a short list of tractable full-scope candidates with exact
sources, prior/duplicate status, concrete proof mechanisms and decisive next steps.
Do not inflate this target with invented, duplicated or publicly resolved questions.
Unpromising candidates need compact rejection entries, not a separate large dossier.

The solving lane should sustain a promising universal proof/counterexample route
beyond one failed shortcut or finite sweep. Pivot promptly when a target hides a
famous hard problem and there is no new mechanism. Use scout shortlists to feed
subsequent solving assignments. Root prioritizes mathematical work and targeted
verification over repetitive administrative rewriting. Reuse verified immutable
source/index references; do not recursively duplicate historical evidence trees.
Keep source fidelity, scientific integrity, resource caps, access discipline,
independent acceptance review and the substantive credit standard unchanged.

Each proposed result needs its precise primary-source statement and quantifiers,
a complete rigorous proof, a literal Lean endpoint with no residual unproved
bridges, independent adversarial review, a documented bounded prior-art and
subsumption investigation, a paper, and a fresh extracted strict replay. Only
propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are allowed in accepted certificates;
no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe/native_decide. No numerical-evidence-as-proof.

Never count a known theorem, public proof/refutation, routine corollary, mere
formalization, wording/domain/endpoint correction, helper, parameter instance,
or another variant of an already credited family. An open MathDB label or empty
solution array is not novelty evidence. Read actual primary theorem bodies.
Newly created MathDB records 414154–414159 are already answered by our first batch.

Read and reconcile old rejection and lane notes before selecting a target. A
held old candidate may be investigated but receives no credit until all original
objections are resolved. Do not infer missing-source clearance from an abstract.

Use existing cached sources where suitable and verify unstable source/prior-art
claims against live primary sources with explicit dates/access limits. Respect
rate limits, robot checks and access controls. No browser/account mutations,
new external messages, publishing or uploads are authorized in this research
phase. Preserve exact URLs/hashes and candid failures.

Before significant new discovery investment or acceptance, check the CURRENT
public proof registries as well as immutable cached snapshots. Record current
head, exact statement/scope and relevant commit/publication chronology. A grep
of an old pinned tree alone cannot clear live prior art. Later independent
public counterparts and our own already credited publications are not prior
proofs merely because they are now searchable; compare chronology and content.
Research delegates must not open preview/browser tabs unless the current user
request specifically authorizes browser work; use public HTTP/search otherwise.
